title: Pasta with Cream Sauce, Poultry and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: A home‑cooked pasta dish featuring a smooth cream sauce, bite‑size pieces of chicken breast and a mix of vegetables (carrot, broccoli, bell pepper). The pasta supplies quick‑release carbs, while the chicken and veggies add protein, vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cream sauce is often made with a roux of flour and low‑fat cream, making it lighter than classic Alfredo.
Chicken breast is one of the leanest meats, low in fat and high in high‑quality protein.
Broccoli is rich in vitamin C and phytochemicals that support the body’s detox pathways.
Cooking pasta al dente preserves its texture and lowers its glycemic impact.
A homemade recipe lets you control salt levels and add favorite herbs such as basil or paprika.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables contribute vitamins A, C, K and minerals like potassium and magnesium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Pasta delivers carbohydrates that are rapidly converted to energy, especially useful after physical activity.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables aids gut motility and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using low‑fat cream keeps the overall saturated‑fat content of the dish modest.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cream can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Undercooked poultry
items.content: Insufficiently cooked chicken may harbor harmful bacteria; ensure an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt in the sauce can increase sodium intake; use it sparingly.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The cream sauce adds calories, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossed with the sauce, chicken and vegetables. Garnish with fresh basil, grated Parmesan or a pinch of black pepper for extra flavor. The dish keeps well in the fridge for up to 2 days and can be reheated in a microwave or skillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the leftovers in an airtight container and refrigerate for no more than 48 hours. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving.
